basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 1.' and it opens 'Vers. 1. Igitur Sara uxor Abraham non genuerat liberos. Quomodo potest Abraham excusari'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 1. Igitur Sara uxor Abraham non genuerat liberos. Quomodo potest Abraham excusari ab adulterio, qui vivente uxore sua ancillae junctus est? Sed necdum promulgata erat lex Evangelii unius uxoris. Simul etiam audierat multiplicandum esse genus suum sicut stellas coeli, sed nesciebat per quam mulierem, quia Saram sterilem noverat. Non ergo fuit in concumbendo libidinosa voluptas, sed pia propagandae prolis charitas. Simul etiam dicendum quia hoc voluntate nimiae cogentiae uxoris fecit quae, | quia ipsa filios habere non poterat, ex alia eos suscipere cupiebat.
